html:
The Guiana Space Centre is the spaceport of France and the European Space Agency at Kourou in French Guiana. France chose the site in 1964, and the first rocket flew in 1968.

Kourou lies close to the equator, so rockets get an extra push from the Earth's spin, and it faces open ocean to the north and east. The Ariane rockets, first launched in 1979, made Europe a leader in launching satellites for paying customers. The James Webb Space Telescope was launched there on an Ariane 5 in 2021.

The centre transformed the small village of Kourou into a town and made space the largest industry in French Guiana. Rockets fly over the old penal islands, which are cleared at each launch. Local protests have argued that the wealth of the centre does little for most people, many of whom live in Cayenne and the poorer west.
